newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed in active trading.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mixed on Tuesday in active trading.
Dealers said focus was mainly on Malaysian over-the-counter (OTC) stocks which saw hectic trading in the afternoon session with profit-taking seen in several counters.
All the top five most active counters were OTC stocks which raked in volumes of between 10 to 20 million units each.

"Volume was quite heavy but profit-taking came in before the close because some of the shares have really run up," said a broker. The UOB-OTC index closed off its day high of 1,297.75 at 1,288.47, up 1.89 points.
Total market volume was 364.4 million shares with 230 gainers against 148 losers.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrial index ended 0.95 point higher at 2,226.30.
Property heavyweights City Developments and Singapore Land saw some buying and both gained 10 cents each to Singapore $13.10 and S$8.45 respectively.

NatSteel rose 14 cents to S$3.50 on moderate volume on news of Southern Steel, in which it has a stake, turning in stronger than expected profits. Losers included SPH foreign which fell 70 cents to S$26.60. - Doreen Siow 65-8703092
